P01.note: Head noun 'the branch office' is singular, so 'was' and the possessive 'its'. 'Borrowers' earlier and 'town' inside the phrase are weak attractors; 'their' is the tempting option because offices are staffed by people.
P01.not_hard_because: Both rules (verb number and pronoun number) point at the same noun, 'the branch office', so solving one hands over the other; only a short prepositional phrase intervenes.

P02.note: Plural head 'cables' and a single completed past moment ('on the morning of the volcano's largest explosion') require past progressive 'were carrying'. 'Have been carrying' is attractive to students who treat ongoing action as present perfect.
P02.not_hard_because: The time phrase 'on the morning of the volcano's largest explosion' plainly fixes a completed past event, and the plural head 'cables' sits right after 'The fiber', so number is not disguised (attractor 'station' is far off).

P03.note: Two copyists share the parts, so the plural possessive 'copyists'' is needed; 'copyist's' is the main distractor but has no single referent. 'Copyists work' reads as a clause and cannot be the subject phrase.
P03.not_hard_because: The first sentence states 'Two copyists' outright, handing over plural number; the only remaining step is apostrophe placement, and 'copyists work' is struck on sight.

P04.note: Plural 'crews' takes 'were'; the thing covered is the observatory's 'lone radio dish', so 'it'. 'Them' is drawn by 'crews', 'farms' and 'tarps'.
P04.not_hard_because: The antecedent is flagged as 'lone radio dish' (lone = singular), and 'crews' is the first word of the subject, so number is visible without parsing; the verb-plural/pronoun-singular split is the same mismatch as most pronoun items here.

P05.note: 'Volunteers' is the plural head ('office' is an attractor), so 'have relined'; the banks belong to the singular 'pond', so 'its'. 'Their' tempts because volunteers is the nearest plural.
P05.not_hard_because: The pond is introduced as 'the farm's only irrigation pond' and 'banks' names a part of a pond, so 'its' is obvious; it repeats the verb-plural/pronoun-singular split of P04, P22, P27.

P06.note: Singular head 'The drill' (attractor 'layers') with present 'while engineers ... decide' requires 'is being run'. 'Was being run' tempts because of 'stalled' and 'sampled' in the past.
P06.not_hard_because: 'while engineers ... decide' immediately after the blank hands over present tense, and 'The drill' is the subject's first noun after a sentence that is entirely about one drill.

P07.note: Singular head 'trial' (attractor 'vaccines') and a bounded past period ('during the first rainy season of the project') call for simple past 'was suspended'. 'Has been suspended' is attractive because the report 'attributes' in present.
P07.not_hard_because: 'A twelve-week trial' opens with the article 'A', giving the number away, and the past-period phrase follows the blank; the present-perfect distractor is the same one that loses in P02, P08, P13, P30.

P08.note: 'The double portrait' is singular ('sisters' is the attractor) and 'during the first half of the eighteenth century' is a closed past period, so 'was obscure'. 'Has been obscure' is tempting only to someone ignoring the period's end and 'Its present fame'.
P08.not_hard_because: 'during the first half of the eighteenth century' right after the blank closes the period, and 'Its present fame' in the next sentence confirms the portrait is no longer obscure; present perfect is the never-key option again.

P09.note: Ellipsis after a semicolon must copy the parallel auxiliary 'was (salvageable)' in past tense with plural 'ceilings': 'were not'. 'Was not' is drawn by 'auditorium' directly before the blank; 'have not' cannot stand for 'salvageable'.
P09.not_hard_because: The parallel clause 'The proscenium was salvageable' sits immediately before and supplies both the verb ('be') and tense; the student only flips number, and 'ceilings' is plainly plural.

P10.note: The elided predicate is 'discharge water at a nearly constant rate' (present, lexical verb), so do-support 'does not' with singular 'geyser'. 'Was not' is attractive because the follow-up sentences report the geyser in the past.
P10.not_hard_because: The parallel clause 'the hot springs ... discharge' supplies a present lexical verb, so do-support and present tense are copied from it; only number changes, and 'the geyser' is singular. Same elliptical template as P09, P12, P31.

P11.note: Compound subject 'The fresco and the gilded screen' is plural; 'unless the parish council installs' is present, so 'are darkening'. 'Is darkening' is drawn by 'chancel' right before the blank.
P11.not_hard_because: The 'and' joining two nouns at the head of the subject is the most familiar plural signal, and 'unless ... installs' after the blank hands over the present tense.

P12.note: Ellipsis of 'are eligible' requires 'are not'; 'the unemployed' (adjective as plural noun) takes a plural verb. 'Is not' tempts a student who reads 'the unemployed' as a mass/singular; 'have not' misses the copula.
P12.not_hard_because: The noun directly before the blank, 'districts', is plural and agrees with the key, so a proximity reader gets it right without knowing the 'the unemployed' rule; the parallel 'are eligible' supplies the verb.

P13.note: Plural 'ceilings' and past 'unless the full council voted' require 'were provisional'. 'Have been provisional' tempts because the opening sentence is present-tense generalisation.
P13.not_hard_because: 'blocks', the noun right before the blank, is plural like the head, so number is not tested in practice; 'voted' in the following clause hands over the past tense.

P14.note: Singular 'archive' takes 'has reunited'; what was reunited is the plural 'baptismal registers', so 'them'. 'It' tempts if read as the parish or the run.
P14.not_hard_because: 'reunited' only makes sense of something divided, and 'registers ... were divided' is the one plural antecedent; verb singular/pronoun plural repeats the mismatch pattern of the other pronoun grids.

P15.note: 'The crypt' is singular (attractor 'transepts'), so 'was bypassed'; the agents are the plural 'pilgrims', so 'by them'. 'By it' (the shrine) is semantically absurd.
P15.not_hard_because: 'by it' has no sensible singular agent (a shrine cannot bypass a crypt), so the pronoun half is free and the verb half has the head noun 'crypt' immediately after 'but the'.

P16.note: Two independent clauses ('a stony meteorite ... left a circular opening' / 'a ring ... refroze'), the second not explaining the first, so a semicolon. The comma splice A is attractive because 'a ring ... around its rim' first reads like an appositive to 'opening'.
P16.not_hard_because: Once the reader finds the second finite verb 'refroze', the boundary is a textbook semicolon; the colon is weak because the ring's refreezing does not elaborate the opening.

P17.note: Plural 'goats' (attractor 'dairy') takes 'devour'; the plant devoured is singular 'Giant hogweed', echoed by 'its sap', so 'it'. 'Them' tempts via 'goats' or 'blisters'.
P17.not_hard_because: 'its sap' in the same clause already uses a singular pronoun for hogweed, so the pronoun is copied; verb-plural/pronoun-singular again matches the cross-item mismatch tell.

P18.note: 'Cattle' is a plural-only noun, and 'provided that the animals drink' is present, so 'are safe'. 'Is safe' tempts students who treat 'cattle' as a mass noun; 'farms' is plural and does not help the distractor.
P18.not_hard_because: 'the animals drink' after the blank renames cattle as explicitly plural and hands over the present tense in one phrase.

P19.note: One mayor ('a single mayor') owns the plans, so singular possessive 'mayor's'. 'Mayors'' tempts only via 'the next administration'.
P19.not_hard_because: The passage says 'a single mayor' outright, and two of the three distractors lack any apostrophe before the noun 'plans', so it reduces to a one-step singular/plural possessive pick.

P20.note: Singular head 'hum' (attractor 'fans', right before the blank) with past 'peaked' requires 'was audible'. 'Were audible' is the strong proximity distractor.
P20.not_hard_because: 'peaked' at the end of the sentence hands over past tense, and 'The hum of' opens the subject so the of-phrase attractor is the standard SAT pattern, identical to P06, P07, P08, P21, P30, P32.

P21.note: 'The census' is singular (attractor 'asteroids'); 'if a survey telescope detects' is present habitual, so 'is updated'. 'Was updated' tempts from the past 'began'/'joined' in sentence one.
P21.not_hard_because: 'if a survey telescope detects' after the blank hands over present tense, and 'census of those asteroids' is the textbook head-plus-of-phrase attractor.

P22.note: Plural 'gospel books' takes 'were'; the claim to fame belongs to the abbey (or monastery), so 'its'. 'Their' tempts as a reflexive reading back to the books.
P22.not_hard_because: 'chief claim to fame' cannot belong to the books themselves in a sentence whose subject is the books, so 'its' (the abbey) is forced; verb plural/pronoun singular repeats the mismatch of P04, P05, P27.

P23.note: The participle 'reappeared' (five words past the blank, after the parenthetical 'by all accounts never') needs perfect 'has', and the head 'rash' is singular despite the appositive 'blisters'. 'Have' is the strong distractor from 'blisters'; 'is/are' fail only once 'reappeared' is located.

P24.note: 'The museum's sole archivist' is singular ('sole'), so 'is digitizing'; what is digitized is 'six hundred recordings', so 'them'. 'It' tempts via the dialect or the museum.
P24.not_hard_because: 'sole archivist' flags singular and 'one cassette at a time' right after the blank signals a plural set being worked through, so both halves are signposted; the verb/pronoun number mismatch is the shared tell.

P25.note: 'Drawn in the barn nearest the duck pond' identifies which samples were retested, so it is restrictive and takes no punctuation. A (comma) is attractive because a nonrestrictive participle looks natural, but it would mean all samples were retested, contradicting 'only'.
P25.not_hard_because: 'only' before the noun and 'To settle the question cheaply' both announce that a subset is being picked out, which makes the restrictive reading obvious; D's comma splitting 'drawn' from its phrase is rejected on sight.

P26.note: 'Each' before a compound subject ('graft and cutting') makes it singular, and 'before the growers recognized' fixes past: 'was developing'. 'Were developing' is strong because 'and' plus the plural 'trays' right before the blank both push plural.

P27.note: Plural 'survey teams' takes 'are tracking'; the plumes come from the only erupting vent, singular, so 'its'. 'Their' is strong because 'the older volcanoes' sits directly before the blank, and only reading 'only active vent' rules it out.

P28.note: Singular 'a camera' takes 'records'; reactions belong to the plural 'seated infants', so 'their'. 'Its' tempts via 'stage' or 'camera'.
P28.not_hard_because: A camera and a stage cannot have 'reactions', so the plural infants are the only sensible owner, and 'a camera' opens the clause with a singular article; it is the one pronoun grid whose verb and pronoun numbers match P01's pattern in reverse, otherwise the same template.

P29.note: The text after the colon is a direct, inverted question ('in which language should ... be taught'), so it ends with a question mark, and 'Their answers' starts a new sentence. D (period) is the strongest distractor: correct boundary, wrong end mark.
P29.not_hard_because: The inversion 'should the first reading lessons be' and 'put a single question to parents' announce a direct question, so the question mark is signposted; A and C are obvious splice/run-on errors once the boundary is seen.

P30.note: Plural 'Applications' (attractor 'employer') with past 'if the paperwork arrived' requires 'were routed'. 'Was routed' is drawn by 'employer' directly before the blank.
P30.not_hard_because: 'arrived' and 'had withdrawn' in the following clause hand over past tense, and 'Applications' is the sentence's first word; same head-plus-of-phrase-plus-conditional template as P13 and P21.

P31.note: Ellipsis of 'withstood' copies the parallel 'has withstood', so present perfect auxiliary in plural: 'have not'. 'Do not' is the strong distractor for readers who supply 'resist scab'.
P31.not_hard_because: The parallel clause 'a single heirloom russet apple has withstood' supplies the auxiliary 'has' to copy, and 'cultivars' (plural) immediately precedes the blank; fourth instance of the same elliptical template (P09, P10, P12).

P32.note: Singular 'rivalry' (attractor 'bands') with present habitual 'after the adjudicators announce ... each September' requires 'is chronicled'. 'Are chronicled' tempts via 'bands' right before the blank.
P32.not_hard_because: 'announce ... each September' after the blank hands over present habitual tense, and 'The rivalry among' is the standard head-plus-prepositional-phrase attractor seen in P20 and P21.

tells: Verb/pronoun 2x2 grids (P01, P04, P05, P14, P15, P17, P22, P24, P27, P28): in 9 of 10 the key is the option whose verb number DIFFERS from its pronoun number (P04 were/it, P05 have/its, P14 has/them, P15 was/them, P17 devour/it, P22 were/its, P24 is/them, P27 are/its, P28 records/their); only P01 (was/its) matches. A test-taker can eliminate the two matched-number options in nearly every grid without finding either antecedent, leaving a coin flip or better.

Present-perfect options never win: 'has been/have been ...' loses in every tense grid where it appears (P02, P07, P08, P13, P30), and 'has not/have not' loses except where the parallel clause itself is present perfect (P31). A student can strike present perfect on sight.

Subject-verb items almost all use one shape: singular or plural head + of/among/in phrase whose noun has the opposite number and sits right before the blank (P06, P07, P08, P11, P20, P21, P26, P30, P32). The key is always the option that does NOT agree with the word immediately before the blank in these items, so 'pick the opposite of the nearest noun' scores them.

Tense in the 2x2 tense/number grids is handed over by a verb in a trailing subordinate clause (unless/if/after/while/before/provided that) in P06, P11, P13, P18, P20, P21, P26, P30, P32: find that verb's tense and copy it.

Elliptical items (P09, P10, P12, P31): the key always copies the auxiliary/verb type of the parallel clause and only flips number; 'have not' and 'do not' variants lose unless the parallel clause uses that auxiliary.
near_duplicates: verb number plus pronoun number 2x2 grid, mismatched numbers
elliptical second clause copying the parallel auxiliary
head plus attractor noun with tense set by a trailing if/unless clause
present tense set by a trailing while/unless/provided/after clause with an attractor noun
singular versus plural possessive with the number stated in the passage
clause-boundary punctuation between two independent clauses
